Q: Why does TypeScript infer string instead of a literal type for object properties, but not for const variables? A:

You could simply create another type, and store the hardcode the string values of the possible types of event trigger you expect, e.g., "click" | "keypress" in your case

Then, when using the Event type, instead of trying all the possible mutations, just use one object with the hardcoded strings from earlier as the type of the "kind" in it.

Side note: use type for strings and hardcoded values and interface for object typing as a convention

Q: Make Youtube API order : date go on chronological order A:

The API doesn't expose an ascending date option order=date is fixed to descending and there's no dateAsc value. The standard workaround is to fetch with order=date + publishedAfter (and optionally publishedBefore), page through everything once, then reverse the list client-side.

from googleapiclient.discovery import build

youtube = build("youtube", "v3", developerKey=API_KEY)

def videos_since(channel_id, since_iso):
    items, token = [], None
    while True:
        resp = youtube.search().list(
            part="snippet",
            channelId=channel_id,
            type="video",
            order="date",            # newest first — we'll flip it
            publishedAfter=since_iso, # e.g. "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
            maxResults=50,
            pageToken=token,
        ).execute()
        items.extend(resp["items"])
        token = resp.get("nextPageToken")
        if not token:
            break
    return list(reversed(items))     # oldest → newest

Q: Apache AH00526 Syntax Error A:

In Apache 2.4 you don't use 2.2 directives.

Remove all "Order/Deny/Allow/Satisfy" directives and just use:

Require

Following your example:

<Files ~ "^\.ht">
        Require all denied
</Files>

Please see upgrading for further changes regarding 2.4 version.

Q: Unable to Access RDS with JDBC in AWS A:

It could be that your instance is in a VPC and your RDS instance isn't set up in a VPC subnet group.

If you want to connect to an RDS instance from a server instance in a VPC, your RDS instance has to be deployed in a VPC subnet.

http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_VPC.CreateDBSubnetGroup.html
